94.description: Washington, D.C. – Today, after Senate Democrats voted against a procedural step to begin consideration of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act, Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott (R-S.C.) spoke on the Senate floor and called out Democrats for playing politics with bipartisan legislation. The GENIUS Act, a bill to establish the first ever regulatory framework for payment stablecoins, was the result of months of bipartisan negotiations and extensive consultation with industry participants, academic experts, and government stakeholders. After considering dozens of amendments to the bill, Chairman Scott successfully advanced the legislation out of the Banking Committee in March with every Republican and five Democrats supporting it.

145.title: Chairman Scott Applauds Scott Turner’s Confirmation as Secretary of Housing and Urban Development
145.description:
Washington, D.C. – Today, the Senate voted to confirm Scott Turner as President Trump’s Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) by a vote of 55-44. Following the vote, Chairman Tim Scott (R-S.C.) spoke on the Senate floor to highlight Secretary Turner’s life story, qualifications to lead HUD, and their share goal of addressing the housing crisis and increasing access to quality, affordable housing opportunities for Americans across the country.

During Secretary Turner’s hearing before the Senate Banking Committee, Chairman Scott highlighted Mr. Turner’s record and leadership directing investments in Opportunity Zones, Chairman Scott’s initiative under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act to increase development in economically distressed communities. Chairman Scott noted he looks forward to working with Secretary Turner to cut bureaucratic red tape, advance commonsense housing solutions, and put more Americans on the path to homeownership.

1.title: Warren Calls for AI Safety, Microchip Export Controls Ahead of President Xi State Visit
1.description: Today, U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, joined Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), Senator Andy Kim (D-N.J.), and Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.) in speaking to reporters about the need for commonsense AI safety regulations and export controls on microchips ahead of Chinese President Xi’s arrival in Washington, D.C. for an official state visit this afternoon.

2.title: Warren Delivers Remarks Ahead of TRIA Reauthorization, CFPB Director and Commerce, HUD Nominee Votes
2.description: Today, U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, delivered opening remarks ahead of committee votes on re-authorizating the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act (TRIA) Program as well as President Trump’s nominations of Brian Johnson to be Director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), Abby Warren to be Commerce Assistant Secretary for Export Administration, Jeffrey Ledbetter to be Inspector General of the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), and Irving Dennis to be HUD Chief Financial Officer.

3.title: Warren Seeks to Stop Trump’s Self-Dealing, End Presidential Corruption in Banking
3.description: U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee urged her Senate colleagues to give unanimous consent to pass the Ending Presidential Corruption in Banking Act. The effort comes in light of recent news that World Liberty Trust Company, a bank owned in part by President Trump and his family, received preliminary approval for a federal banking charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. Despite clear national security risks, money laundering vulnerabilities, and a lack of competent management, the Trump-controlled federal banking agency approved the charter.

4.title: Warren Remarks Ahead of Clarity Act Procedural Vote on Senate Floor
4.description: Today on the Senate floor, U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, gave remarks on the Senate floor ahead of a procedural vote on the Republican-led Digital Asset Market Clarity (Clarity) Act.

Maxine Waters (D-CA-43), and Democrats will hold a press conference highlighting the passage of the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, the biggest housing bill in over 30 years – and calling on Trump to sign the bill after he delayed its signing. Earlier this year, Senate Democrats launched the 2026 Costs Initiative, a sustained push focused on lowering housing costs and addressing the economic pressures facing working families. Senators Warren and Schumer released a “Broken Promises” analysis detailing President Trump’s failure to meet his commitments to lower housing costs.

80.title: Senate Banking Democrats Investigate Trump-Musk Attack on American Consumers
80.description:
Tuesday, February 25, 2025, U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), the top Democrat on the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affair Committee will convene a forum to investigate the Trump-Musk Attack on American Consumers. The forum will focus on the consequences of President Trump’s and Elon Musk’s efforts to eliminate the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) - an agency that has returned over $21 billion to families scammed by financial institutions. 

Panelists for the forum include: 
-Andrea Campbell, Attorney General of Massachusetts. Just 4 months ago, the CFPB and AG Campbell won a $50M judgment against a scammy, MA-based credit repair company. This company was charging up to $200/month by promising to increase consumers’ credit scores by 90 points in 90 days and scammed consumers out of $32M.
-Lorelei Salas, former CFPB Director of Supervision Policy
-Stacey McCall, a retired Army veteran of 20 years from Maryland, who was being forced to pay for a Toyota vehicle she couldn’t drive until the CFPB stepped in
-Marette Gillen, a mortgage originator from Texas, who has seen firsthand how the CFPB has positively impacted her industry

Senator Warren also invited Elon Musk to give him the opportunity to provide a public explanation for his role in preventing the CFPB from protecting families from getting scammed, and to answer questions about his financial interest in dismantling the agency.

Individuals with disabilities who require an auxiliary aid or service, including closed captioning service for webcast hearings, should contact the committee clerk at 202-224-7391 at least three business days in advance of the hearing date.

175.title: Federal Reserve Chair Powell's Nomination Hearing
175.description:
THE COMMITTEE ON BANKING, HOUSING, AND URBAN AFFAIRS will meet in OPEN SESSION, HYBRID FORMAT to conduct a hearing on the following nomination: The Honorable Jerome H. Powell, of Maryland, to be Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.

Pursuant to guidance from the CDC and OAP, Senate office buildings are not open to the public other than official business visitors and credentialed press at this time. Accordingly, in-person visitors cannot be accommodated at this briefing. We encourage the public to utilize the Committee’s livestream of the hearing, available on the website at http://www.banking.senate.gov.

All hearings are webcast live and will not be available until the hearing starts. Individuals with disabilities who require an auxiliary aid or service, including closed captioning service for webcast hearings, should contact the committee clerk at 202-224-7391 at least three business days in advance of the hearing date.

1.title: Crapo Urges Colleagues to Support Bureau Nominee
1.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, speaks on the Senate Floor in favor of Ms. Kathy Kraninger to be the Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection.

2.title: Crapo on Elad Roisman Nomination to the SEC
2.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, delivers remarks on the Senate Floor regarding Elad Roisman's nomination to serve on the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

3.title: Crapo Statement at Nomination Hearing
3.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, gives opening remarks at a nomination hearing to consider Mr. Elad L. Roisman, of Maine, to be a Member of the Securities and Exchange Commission; Mr. Michael R. Bright, of the District of Columbia, to be President of the Government National Mortgage Association; Ms. Rae Oliver, of Virginia, to be Inspector General, U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development; and Dr. Dino Falaschetti, of Montana, to be Director, Office of Financial Research, U.S. Department of the Treasury.

4.title: What Crapo's Banking Bill Means for Idaho
4.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, discusses what his Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act (S. 2155) means for community banks, credit unions, and Idaho's economy.

5.title: President Signs Crapo's Banking Bill Into Law
5.description: President Trump signs Idaho Senator Mike Crapo's "Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act" (S. 2155) into law. The bipartisan bill right-sizes regulations for community banks, credit unions, mid-size banks and regional banks, and includes important consumer protections.

6.title: Crapo on Jelena McWilliams to Lead FDIC
6.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, urges his Senate colleagues to confirm Jelena McWilliams to lead the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation.

7.title: Crapo on Brian Montgomery to lead the FHA
7.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, delivers remarks on the Senate Floor, encouraging his colleagues to support the nomination of Brian Montgomery to lead the Federal Housing Administration. Montgomery was confirmed 74-23.

8.title: Crapo at CFPB Hearing with Mulvaney
8.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, asks about creating an independent Inspector General for the CFPB, and the increasing amounts of big data collected by the CFPB.

9.title: Crapo on Senate Passage of the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act
9.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, delivers remarks on the Senate Floor before final passage of the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act.

10.title: Time to Right-Size Regulation for Main Street
10.description: Banking Committee Chairman Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) explains why the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act is an important piece of legislation for Main Street financial institutions.

11.title: Regulatory Burden Directly Impacts Our States
11.description: Senator Crapo discusses the regulatory burden Dodd-Frank has imposed on Idaho's small financial institutions, and how his legislation, the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act (S. 2155) can help.

12.title: Crapo Discusses Regulatory Relief Bill on Fox Business
12.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) joins Charles Payne on Fox Business’s Making Money about Dodd-Frank’s impact on Idaho’s Main Street financial institutions,

13.title: Crapo on Bipartisan Regulatory Relief Package
13.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, joined several of his colleagues from the Committee to discuss his bill, the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act, which is being debated on the Senate Floor this week.

14.title: Relief for Main Street
14.description: Community banks and credit unions have long struggled to keep up with the ever-increasing regulatory demands coming out of Washington. The reforms in the bipartisan Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief, and Consumer Protection Act will help small businesses access the resources they need to invest and hire more workers.

15.title: Crapo Touts Benefits of the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act (S. 2155)
15.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, discusses the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act, S. 2155, with Senate Leadership.

16.title: U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs

17.title: Crapo Supports Powell for Federal Reserve Chairman
17.description: Senator Mike Crapo (R-ID), Chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, delivers remarks on the Senate Floor, encouraging colleagues to support the nomination of Jerome Powell for Federal Reserve Chairman.

18.title: Chairman Crapo at S. 2155 Markup
18.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Chairman of the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, delivers opening remarks at a hearing to consider S. 2155, the "Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief and Consumer Protection Act." The bill was approved by the Committee by a bipartisan vote of 16-7.

19.title: Banking Chairman Crapo on Federal Reserve, Regulatory Reform
19.description: Banking Committee Chairman Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) talks to Bloomberg's Kevin Cirilli about the President's recent nominee to lead the Federal Reserve, Jerome Powell, and the Banking Committee's regulatory relief efforts.

20.title: Crapo: Congress to Determine Future of Housing Finance Reform
20.description: Ranking Member Crapo asks FHFA Director Mel Watt to confirm that the role of the conservator of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac is to be a bridge builder, and that Congress should determine the role of Fannie and Freddie in our housing market in the U.S.

21.title: Crapo at FHFA Oversight Hearing
21.description: Ranking Member Crapo (R-Idaho) delivers remarks at a Senate Banking Committee hearing on Federal Housing Finance Agency oversight. In his remarks, Crapo notes several actions that FHFA Director Mel Watt has taken over the last year, saying that "While I have serious concerns with some of these ideas individually, perhaps my largest concern is that collectively, they appear to feed a perception that the old, failed status quo is slowly beginning to take hold again."

22.title: Crapo: Operation Choke Point Negatively Affects Legitimate Business Relationships
22.description: At a Senate Banking Committee hearing on consumer financial protection, Ranking Member Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) raises concerns with the Department of Justice-led Operation Choke Point, which has been targeting legitimate and legally-operating businesses and negatively impacting their banking relationships.

23.title: Crapo to Regulators: Commit to Regulatory Review Process that Produces Results
23.description: Senator Crapo tells regulators that they are not successfully eliminating the perception that the Administration is not targeting specific industries via Operation Choke Point. He goes on to emphasize the need to reduce the regulatory burden on community banks, many of which can be done without Congressional authority. Crapo requests the regulators to make a concerted effort to ensure that their review, pursuant to the Economic Growth and Regulatory Paperwork Reduction Act of 1996, produce meaningful results.

24.title: Tarullo Says SIFI Threshold Should be Raised
24.description: Responding to questioning from Ranking Member Crapo, Federal Reserve Board Member Daniel Tarullo stated that the threshold for determining what constitutes a systemically important financial institution (SIFI) should be moved “below the largest banks,” moving his previously stated position that the level should be much lower.

25.title: Crapo: “Too Big to Fail” now “Too Small to Succeed”
25.description: At a Senate Banking Committee hearing on small depository institutions, Ranking Member Mike Crapo discusses the disproportionate effect that regulations stemming from Dodd-Frank have had on community banks around the country, and particularly in rural communities in Idaho.

26.title: Regulatory Review and Relief for Community Banks
26.description: Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, questions federal regulators regarding the Economic Growth and Regulatory Paperwork Reduction Act of 1996 (EGRPRA)-mandated interagency review of existing regulations to identify “outdated, unnecessary, or unduly burdensome regulations.”

27.title: Wall Street Reform: Assessing and Enhancing the Financial Regulatory System
27.description: Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, delivers opening remarks during a Dodd-Frank hearing. Senator Crapo stresses the cumulative costs that Dodd-Frank rulemakings have had on consumers and small financial institutions.

28.title: Crapo on Fed's Quantitative Easing
28.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo discusses the Federal Reserve's unconventional monetary policy in a weekly radio call with Idaho reporters. As part of his oversight role as Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, Crapo had recently met with the Federal Reserve's Chair, Janet Yellen.

29.title: Crapo on America's Fiscal Solvency
29.description: In a radio interview with KIDO's Kevin Miller, Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Banking Committee, discusses the state of our economy, noting that at some point, we're going to largely feel the consequences of the Federal Reserve's unconventional monetary policy.

30.title: Senate Passes Bipartisan TRIA
30.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, discusses the important reforms included in the Terrorism Risk Insurance Reauthorization Program, or TRIA. This reauthorization legislation included reforms to increase taxpayer protection in the event of a future act of terrorism, while strengthening economic resilience in the event of future attacks.

31.title: Community Bank Experience Needed on Federal Reserve Board
31.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, discusses his support for an amendment to the Terrorism Risk Insurance Reauthorization Act (TRIA) that will ensure the President nominates an individual with strong community banking experience to fill a position on the Federal Reserve Board.

32.title: Crapo on the Terrorism Risk Insurance Reauthorization Act
32.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Comnmittee, takes to the Senate Floor to promote the passage of S.2244, the Terrorism Risk Insurance Reauthorization Act, or TRIA. TRIA passed by a strong bipartisan vote of 93-4.

33.title: Crapo Questions Fed Chair Janet Yellen on Monetary Policy
33.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, questions Fed Chair Janet Yellen on rate hikes and the normalization of monetary policy.

34.title: Crapo at Monetary Policy Report
34.description: At the Federal Reserve's semi-annual monetary policy report to Congress, Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Banking Committee, states the need to fill vacant Fed Board positions with someone who has community banking experience. He also expresses opposition to quantitative easing, and the importance of balancing open communication with the ability to preserve flexibility.

35.title: Crapo: How Can We Help Small Companies in Secondary Markets?
35.description: At a hearing on high frequency trading and equity market strucutre, Ranking Member Crapo says: "According to reports, the JOBS act has been very helpful in aiding companies under our capital and equities markets, but there's still a lot of concern that smaller companies are unable to tap into our equity markets."

36.title: Crapo on Equity Market Structure Weakness
36.description: Ranking Member Mike Crapo asks witnesses where they believe the greatest weakness in today's market structure is.

37.title: Crapo at High Frequency Trading Hearing
37.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, delivers opening remarks during a hearing held to examine equity market structure.

38.title: Crapo: Lack of Transparency in SIFI Designation Process
38.description: Banking Committee Ranking Member Mike Crapo asserts that FSOC should either publish a list of criteria it uses to designate a firm as a systematically important financial institution (SIFI), or provide a detailed analysis of why a firm has been designated, so other firms have some guidelines on whether or not they could become SIFIs. Crapo asks Lew if FSOC would be willing to publish specific criteria for public viewing.

39.title: Opening Remarks at FSOC Annual Report
39.description: Banking Committee Ranking Member Mike Crapo raises several concerns with the Financial Stability Oversight Council, including infighting among U.S. financial regulators, international coordination on financial reform, the non-bank SIFI designation process, and the role asset managers play in our financial system.

40.title: Crapo Talks Massive Federal Database on Weekly Teleconference
40.description: Senator Crapo talks about recent efforts underway at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and Federal Housing Finance Agency to create a massive database that will include personally identifiable information about consumers, including name, address, social security number, religion, and even "life events."

41.title: How is the CFPB involved in Operation Choke Point?
41.description: At the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's semi-annual report to Congress, Ranking Member Mike Crapo asks CFPB Director Richard Cordray how the CFPB is involved in Operation Choke Point, if at all. Operation Choke Point is an effort by the Department of Justice and federal banking regulators to pressure banks into ending relationships with legally-operating payday lenders and gun store retailers.

42.title: Crapo to CFPB: Unnecessary Invasion of Privacy
42.description: Ranking Member Crapo questions CFPB Director Cordray about whether the vast amounts of data collected for the National Mortgage Database can be reverse-engineered to identify individuals.  One of the project managers for the database has been previously quoted saying "It is easy to identify the people in our database."

43.title: Crapo on CFPB's Massive Data Collection
43.description: Ranking Member Crapo asks CFPB Director Richard Cordray about a vast expansion of the National Mortgage Database, a collective undertaking by the CFPB and FHFA.  Crapo specifically asks whether any of the information in the expanded database will be personally identifiable.

44.title: Crapo on CFPB's Semi-Annual Report to Congress
44.description: U.S. Senator Mike Crapo (R-Idaho), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, delivers remarks during the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's semi-annual report to Congress.  Crapo addresses the CFPB's rulemaking agenda, big data collection, and recent discrimination charges at the Bureau.

45.title: Crapo on Need for Housing Finance Reform
45.description: Senator Crapo talks about his recently-introduced bipartisan legislation to overhaul the housing finance market. The legislation will wind down Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, end the government domination of the housing market and promote the re-entry of private capital into our housing finance system. To read more about Senator Crapo's legislation, go to www.banking.senate.gov.

46.title: Crapo Questions Fed VP Nominee Stan Fischer on Monetary Policy
46.description: Senate Banking Committee Ranking Member Mike Crapo, R-Idaho, asks Dr. Stan Fischer whether he believes the Fed faces significant challenges in unwinding its economic support programs without disrupting the economy. Fischer replies that the Fed will monitor the financial markets' reactions as it winds down its bond purchase program.

47.title: Crapo Joins Squawk on the Street to Talk Housing Reform
47.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, joins Rick Santelli on CNBC's Squawk on the Street to talk comprehensive housing finance reform.

48.title: Crapo Talks Housing Finance Reform on Bloomberg TV
48.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, joins Bloomberg TV's Chief Washington Correspondent Peter Cook to talk about nominations to the Federal Reserve Board and housing finance reform. Crapo and Chairman Johnson recently announced an agreement to comprehensively reform the housing market.

49.title: Crapo at Confirmation Hearing
49.description: U.S. Senator Mike Crapo (R-Idaho), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, delivered the following remarks during a Banking Committee hearing to consider several nominations to the Federal Reserve Board, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, and the National Credit Union Administration Board.

50.title: Crapo Talks Housing Finance Reform on Willis Report
50.description: Banking Committee Ranking Member Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) joins Gerri Willis on Fox Business's "The Willis Report" to talk about a recent bipartisan agreement to comprehensively reform the housing finance system.

51.title: Crapo on Challenges for Rural Transportation
51.description: At a Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee hearing on "MAP-21 Reauthorization: The Federal Role and Current Challenges to Public Transportation," Ranking Member Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) asks witnesses what they think the biggest challenges are facing rural states' transportation issues.

52.title: Crapo on MAP-21 Reauthorization
52.description: At a Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee hearing on "MAP-21 Reauthorization: The Federal Role and Current Challenges to Public Transportation," Ranking Member Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) delivers opening remarks, noting that it is important to fix the flaws that currently exist in portions of teh Highway Trust Fund.

53.title: Crapo to Yellen on GSE Reform
53.description: At a Senate Banking Committee hearing on the Semiannual Monetary Policy Report to Congress, Ranking Member Crapo asks Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen to discuss the need to bring private capital back into the market.  Yellen strongly urges Congress to address GSE reform, noting that private capital should return in meaningful amounts to the industry. Other items discussed include Dodd-Frank implementation and cross-border issues.

54.title: Crapo at Semiannual Monetary Policy Report Hearing
54.description: Opening Statement: Senator Mike Crapo, ranking member of the Senate Banke, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, delivers opening remarks at a hearing entitled "The Semiannual Monetary Policy Report to Congress." The witness was Janet Yellen, Chair of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.  This was Chair Yellen's first time appearing before the Committee as Chair.

55.title: Crapo on TRIA Reauthorization
55.description: Opening Statement: At the U.S. Senate Banking Committee's second hearing on the reauthorization of the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act, Ranking Member Mike Crapo notes that in order to limit the economic and physical impact of any future terrorist attack on the U.S., we must get TRIA right.

56.title: Crapo Talks Quantitative Easing at Budget Committee
56.description: Senator Crapo discusses his concerns with the Federeal Reserve's unconventional monetary policy, asking each witness what they think the risks of inflation are, or what the effect of ending QE will be.  Witnesses include David A. Rosenberg, Mark Zandi and Robert Greenstean.

57.title: Crapo Questions Witnesses at Oversight Hearing on Data Security
57.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Banking Committee, questions witnesses during an oversight hearing on financial stability and data security.

58.title: Crapo on Financial Stability and Data Security
58.description: At a Banking Committee oversight hearing on financial stability and data security, Ranking Member Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) reminds regulators that their data collection needs to be as safe and secure as possible so consumers will not have to fear a data breach at the federal government level, and so they do not have to fear the misuse of that data being collected.

59.title: Crapo Questions Export Import Bank President, Fred Hochberg
59.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, questions Ex-Im Bank President Fred Hochberg about the bank's activities, particularly on the Bank's activities regarding small businesses.

60.title: Crapo on CFPB Data Collection, Privacy
60.description: Senator Crapo discusses his concerns with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) and the vast amount of data the agency is collecting, and provides an update on the Government Accountability Office's audit of the bureau.

61.title: Crapo at Export-Import Bank Reauthorization Hearing
61.description: Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, delivers opening remarks at a hearing entitled "Oversight and Reauthorization of the Export-Import Bank of the United States." At this hearing, the Committee continued its ongoing oversight of the recent activities of the Export-Import Bank.

62.title: Crapo on MAP-21 Progress and Implementation
62.description: Senator Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, delivers opening remarks at a hearing entitled, "Progress Report on Public Transportation under MAP-21."

63.title: Crapo Talks Jobs, Economy with Kevin Miller
63.description: Senator Crapo, Ranking Member of the Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, talks unemployment with Kevin Miller of KIDO Radio, noting that the Federal Reserve's contiunous printing of money exacerbates the problem and does not address the underlying problems with our stagnant economy.

64.title: Crapo Talks CFPB and Data Privacy with Kevin Miller
64.description: Senator Crapo, Ranking Member of the Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, joins Kevin Miller of KIDO to talk about hot issues, including personal privacy and data collection.  Crapo has long been concerned with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureua's massive data collection undertaking.

65.title: Exactly How do you Define "Nuclear Sanctions"?
65.description: Ranking Member Crapo asks Wendy Sherman, Under Secretary of State, how exactly we are to distinguish between sanctions and what constitutes "nuclear" sanctions vs. other sanctions.

66.title: Crapo: FHFA Director Should be Apolitical Technocrat
66.description: As the Senate voted on Mel Watt to be Director of the FHFA, Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, took to the Senate Floor to explain why Representative Watt was a poor choice for this particular position. Namely, as the head of a highly complex agency with a multi-trillion dollar portfolio, the Director should be politically independent and highly trained in this field.

67.title: How can we move private capital into the market?
67.description: Ranking Member Crapo asks Mr. Sandeep Bordia, Head of Residential & Commercial Credit Strategy, Barclays Capital, to explain the need for having a wide variety of options for moving mortgage credit risk into the private market as opposed to limited options.

68.title: Crapo on Risk Sharing in New Housing Market
68.description: Ranking member Mike Crapo delivers opening remarks at a Banking Committee hearing held to examine the fundamentals of transferring credit risk in a future housing finance system.

69.title: Crapo on the "Joint Plan of Action" With Iran
69.description: At a Banking Committee hearing held to examine administration perspectives on the "Joint Plan of Action" with Iran regarding its nuclear program, Ranking Member Mike Crapo expressed his concerns with the plan, and with imprisoned Idaho Pastor Saeed Abedini.

70.title: Crapo: American Prisoners in Iran Must be Top Priority
70.description: During a Banking Committee hearing on the P5+1 interim nuclear agreement with Iran, Ranking Member Mike Crapo took the opportunity to ask Under Secretary of State Wendy Sherman what was being done to assure the release of American prisoners in Iran, including Idaho's own Pastor Saeed Abedini.

71.title: Crapo on Iran Sanctions, Abedini
71.description: Senator Crapo joins 580 KIDO's Kevin Milller to talk Iran sanctions and Boise Pastor Saeed Abedini.

72.title: Crapo: Policy Perspective on Loan Limits
72.description: At a Banking Committee hearing on housing finance reform and the best structure for a strong, effective regulator, Ranking Member Crapo asks witnesses to explain, from a policy perspective, why we should or shouldn't be setting maximum authorized loans at the highest point possibile or the current limits being discussed.

73.title: Crapo: New Regulator Must Not Serve Duplicative Role
73.description: During a Banking Committee hearing on housing finance reform, Senators question witnesses about the structure of a new regulator. Senator Crapo asks "How do we ensure that we establish a new regulator with the appropriate scope and authority without duplicating efforts and actions of exisiting regulators?"

74.title: Crapo on a Strong Secondary Mortgage Market Regulator
74.description: Ranking Member Crapo delivers opening remarks at a Banking Committee hearing held to explore the current regulatory structure related to the secondary mortgage market and examine issues related to proposed regulatory structures.

75.title: Crapo on the Transition to a New Housing Finance Market
75.description: Ranking Member Mike Crapo's opening statement at a Banking Committee hearing to examine various options for a transition to a new housing finance system that achieves the accessibility, affordability, and stability goals of housing finance reform while minimizing disruptions to both the primary and secondary mortgage markets.

76.title: Crapo on Yellen Vote
76.description: During a Banking Committee Executive Session to consider the nomination of Janet Yellen to be Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Senator Crapo explains that he cannot offer Dr. Yellen his support.  Crapo had previously asked Dr. Yellen repeatdedly how long we can artificially hold or operate monetary policy at extreme levels of quantitative easing.  She gave no indication that, if confirmed, she is prepared to scale back or stop quantitative easing, or adjust the interest rate to an objective metric.

77.title: Size of the Fed's Balance Sheet is Concerning
77.description: At a Senate Banking Committee hearing held to consider the nomination of Janet Yellen to head the Federal Reserve, Ranking Member Mike Crapo asked the nominee to respond to the concerns that quantitative easing has limited impact on economic growth, and is in fact creative very serious risks in our market.

78.title: Crapo: Next Fed Chair Faces Unique Challenges
78.description: In a Banking Committee hearing held to consider the nominatino of Janet Yellen for Federal Reserve Chairman, Ranking Member Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) discusses the need to taper quantitative easing, finalize regulatory rules and address much-needed fixes to Dodd-Frank.

79.title: Crapo: Current Fed Policy Dangerous for the Economy
79.description: During an interview on Bloomberg TV's Market Makers, Idaho Senator Mike Crapo (Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee) talks to Stephanie Ruhle and Peter Cook, outlining his concerns with the Fed's unconventional monetary policy and why it is a deterrent to real fiscal reform in Washington, D.C.

80.title: Crapo: Data Collection Carries Significant Risk
80.description: Ranking Member Crapo follows up on earlier questioning with CFPB Director Richard Cordray regarding personally identifiable information that is collected by the agency. Crapo points out that although data collection by companies and organizations is nothing new, data collection by agencies with the power of the federal government backing them is of serious concern. (11/13/2013)

81.title: Crapo: How Many Consumer Accounts is the Bureau Monitoring?
81.description: In a Senate Banking Committee hearing on the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's semi-annual report to Congress, Ranking Member Crapo (R-Idaho) persistently asks Director Cordray for the specific amount of credit card accounts that the Bureau is following on a monthly basis. After repeated claims from Director Cordray that the agency does not do anything that other agencies aren't doing, Crapo said: "I take your answer to be that it is accurate that the Bureau is collecting information on approximately 900 million individual credit card accounts, and that other agencies are doing the same." (11/13/2013)

82.title: CFPB Must be Treated as Seasoned Regulator
82.description: During a Banking Committee hearing on the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's semi-annual report to Congress, Ranking Member Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) noted the need to hold the CFPB to the same level of accountability as other regulators.  He welcomed the opportunity to evaluate the Bureau's past performance and to discuss the future of the agency. Crapo also noted one of his biggest concerns with the Bureau--its collection of massive amounts of consumer data. (11/13/2013)

83.title: Crapo on Solving our Long-term Fiscal Problems
83.description: At a U.S. Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee hearing with Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke, Ranking Republican Member Mike Crapo highlights the need to address our federal spending problem.   Chairman Bernanke has steadfastly reminded congress that one of the most important risks to our economy is our fiscal situation. (February 26, 2013)

84.title: Crapo Opening Statement at Wall Street Oversight Hearing
84.description: "Implementing the Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act," February 14, 2013.  Senator Crapo delivers opening remarks on the on-going implementation of Dodd-Frank.

86.title: Crapo: Keeping Housing Program Funds Accountable to Taxpayers
86.description: During a Banking Committee hearing on affordable housing options, Ranking Member Crapo focuses on appropriations and how to ensure funds are accountable to taxpayers: "The Housing Trust Fund and Capital Magnet Fund would receive an estimated total of $2.5 billion to $5 billion in annual funding using today's secondary market size.  This represents roughly 10 percent of HUD's annual budget. What kind of safeguards do you think would be appropriate to ensure that these funds remain accountable to Congress and the American taxpayer?"

87.title: Crapo on Options for Affordable Housing
87.description: Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, delivers opening remarks during a housing finance reform hearing focusing on recommendations to provide affordable options for homeownership and rental housing, affordable mortgage credit in rural and underserved communities, and solutions to addressing the cost burdens facing many renters. Crapo noted the importance of promoting responsible housing policies without placing the American taxpayer at risk.

88.title: Crapo on Small Lender Access to Secondary Mortgage Market
88.description: Ranking Member Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) delivers opening remarks during a hearing to discuss the needs of small lenders, including depository institutions and non-bank lenders, to continue to access the secondary mortgage market in a reformed housing finance system. The hearing focused on the components of the current housing finance system, such as infrastructure, technology, and the cash window, that need to be preserved for small lenders in a new housing finance system.

89.title: Crapo on Government Guarantees in Housing Finance Reform
89.description: Ranking Member Crapo asks witnesses a series of questions related to government backstops in housing finance reform.

90.title: Crapo: Must Bring Private Capital Back into Housing Market
90.description: On Thursday, October 31, the full Committee met to focus on the structure of a government guarantee for mortgage-backed securities (MBS). Witnesses addressed how different elements of a government guarantee such as the attachment point and amount and type of private capital standing before the government would influence credit availability and the to-be-announced (TBA) market. They also explored other federal guarantees that could serve as models to protect taxpayers while providing a well-functioning mortgage market and what structures are needed to ensure a stable countercyclical function in the housing finance system.

91.title: Housing Finance Reform Hearing: Consumer Perspective
91.description: During a Banking Committee hearing held to examine housing finance reform from the consumer perspective, Ranking Member Crapo questions witnesses on several topics, including borrower equity, servicer economic incentives and mortgage servicing practices.

92.title: Crapo Statement at Hearing on Essential Housing Finance Reform Elements for Consumers
92.description: At a Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs hearing entitled "Housing Finance Reform: Essentials of a Functioning Housing Finance System for Consumers,"  Ranking Member Mike Crapo emphasizes that done correctly and responsibly, a reformed housing finance system can help millions of families and individuals across the country.

93.title: Ranking Member Crapo on Multifamily Housing Reform
93.description: At a Banking Committee hearing on housing finance reform held to examine essential elements of the multifamily housing finance system, Ranking Member Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) notes that although the multifamily market is much smaller than the single family market, it still serves as a vital source of housing for more than fifteen million American households across the country. There are important lessons to be learned from the enterprises' multifamily activities work continues on reforming the single family market.

94.title: Crapo on Credit Ratings
94.description: Senator Crapo poses a question to various heads of some of the nation's largest financial institutions regarding credit ratings: Which threat is greater--not raising the debt ceiling, or the failure to address our massive debt? Crapo also cites comments from a hearing that morning where he reminded Treasury Secretary Jack Lew that the progress in deficit reduction over recent years is the result of the 2011 debt ceiling negotiations.

95.title: Crapo at Terrorism Risk Insurance Hearing
95.description: At a Banking Committee hearing entitled "Reauthorizing TRIA: The State of the Terrorism Risk Insurance Market," Senator Crapo stresses the importance of examining how well the program is working, and how else Congress might increase private sector participation in the insurance and reinsurance markets.

96.title: Crapo on Housing Finance Reform
96.description: At a hearing entitled "Essential Elements of Housing Finance Reform and Executive Session," Banking Committee Ranking Member Mike Crapo offers opening remarks, indicating that as the process on comprehensive GSE reform moves forward, the Committee must exercise the same bipartisan nature that existed when the FHA Solvency Act of 2013 passed out of Committee.

97.title: Crapo to CFTC on "Path Forward"
97.description: Ranking Member Crapo asks CFTC Chairman Gary Gensler to elaborate on the agreement with the European Commission relating to the joint understanding on a package of meausres for regulating cross-border derivatives, the document commonly being referred to as the "path forward."

98.title: Crapo on Coordination between SEC and CFTC
98.description: Senator Crapo asks Chair White and Chairman Gensler if they agree that they should be improving coordination between the agencies, and if so, what steps they are undertaking to achieve objectives in communiation and coordination.

99.title: Crapo at Financial Markets Oversight Hearing
99.description: Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, delivers opening remarks during a hearing on mitigating systemic risk in financial markets through Wall Street reform.  Witnesses from the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodities Futures Trading Commission testified.  Crapo pointed out the lack of coordination between the two agencies when it comes to regulating securities at home and abroad, and suggested that if the two do not cooperate soon, he would not be surprised if there were calls to merge the two agencies into a single regulator.

100.title: Crapo Questions HUD Assistant Secretary on FHA Reform
100.description: Ranking Member Crapo questions HUD Assistant Secretary Carol Galante during a Banking Committee hearing on the Johnson-Crapo FHA Solvency Act of 2013 legislation.

101.title: Crapo on FHA Solvency Act of 2013
101.description: Ranking Member Crapo delivers opening remarks during a hearing to discuss the Johnson-Crapo FHA Solvency Act of 2013, a bipartisan bill to ensure stability in teh nation's mortgage market and protect taxpayers.

102.title: Crapo: Arguments to Reform CFPB Remain Strong
102.description: Following the Senate's confirmation of Richard Cordray to be Director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Senator Crapo reminds folks that the need for structural reforms at the Bureau are no less critical. The components of its existing structure are a recipe for disaster, and we're beginning to see that with the CFPB's recent data collection effort (for example).  Senator Crapo will continue to fight for structural changes to the CFPB.

103.title: Winding Down the Fed's Balance Sheet
103.description: Ranking Member Crapo asks Chairman Bernanke about keeping the Fed's quantitative easing securities on its balance sheet, and whether he is concerned that the balance sheet could lead to credit mispricing and investors taking on excessive risk.

104.title: Crapo Statement on Monetary Policy Report
104.description: Crapo welcomes Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke to the Banking Committee hearing on the Fed's Semi-Annual Monetary Policy Report to the Congress, saying "It is my hope that this hearing gives us additional insight into the Fed's plans for future reduction of asset purchases and a roadmap for a return to normalized, rules-based monetary policy."

105.title: Crapo: Conservator Must be Apolitical
105.description: Senator Crapo reiterates his concerns with appointing a political figure to head the FHFA.  "Because the conservator has virtually unchecked power to control two multitrillion dollar companies (Fannie and Freddie) and, through them, our entire mortgage market, the conservator must be an apolitical financial regulator with technical expertise and someone who will resist political pressure from all sides of the political spectrum."

106.title: Crapo on the Defense Production Act
106.description: Senator Crapo's opening statement at a hearing entitled "Oversight of the Defense Production Act: Issues and Opportunities for Reauthorization."  A panel of Adminstration witnesses provided an overview of the current programs and projects authorized under the Defense Production Act of 1950.

107.title: Crapo: Data Collection Serious Cause for Concern
107.description: Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, delivers a speech on the Senate Floor detailing the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's massive data collection effort on millions of Americans' spending habits.  Crapo has been engaged in an effort to curb this collection until the agency is made transparent and accountable for how it is using the information, what information is being collected, and how consumers can be assured their privacy is secure.

108.title: Crapo: Data Collection Serious Cause for Concern
108.description: Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, delivers a speech on the Senate Floor detailing the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's massive data collection effort on millions of Americans' spending habits.  Crapo has been engaged in an effort to curb this collection until the agency is made transparent and accountable for how it is using the information, what information is being collected, and how consumers can be assured their privacy is secure.

109.title: Crapo: "I will continue to push for reforms to CFPB"
109.description: Speaking on the Floor of the United States Senate, Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, outlined his serious concerns with the current structure of the CFPB, citing such problems as a massive data collection effort the agency has undertaken on millions of Americans' personal financial data.  Crapo assures the Senate that although Cordray's confirmation is likely, he will continue to fight for reforms that will make the CFPB more transparent and accountable.

110.title: Enzi: "Consumer Protection Must be Balanced with Privacy Protection.'
110.description: Speaking on the Senate Floor regarding the nomination of a director to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Senator Mike Enzi (R-Wyoming) notes the lack of transparency, oversight and accountability at the bureau, and insists that consumer protection must be balanced with privacy protection.

111.title: Enzi: Consumers Deserve "Opt-Out" Option from Data Collection
111.description: Speaking on the Senate Floor regarding the nomination of a director to head the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Senator Enzi (R-Wyoming), a long-time advocate of privacy rights, raises serious concerns with the bureau's practice of collecting massive amounts of consumer financial information without permission.

112.title: Crapo on Implementation of Dodd-Frank
112.description: Ranking Member Crapo delivers opening remarks at a Banking Committee hearing entitled "Mitigating Systemic Risk Through Wall Street Reforms."  The committee heard from four witnesses from the Federal Reserve, FDIC, OCC and Treasury/FSOC.  This July marks the third anniversary since Dodd-Frank became law.

113.title: Crapo talks CFPB on KBLI Radio
113.description: In a radio interview with Mark Richardson (Idaho Falls, KBLI), Senator Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, discusses committee-related issues including the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's data grab of consumers' personal financial information.

114.title: Crapo Discusses Concerns with CFPB
114.description: During his weekly teleconference with Idaho reporters, Senator Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, expresses concerns with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, particularly regarding a new effort headed by the Bureau to collect massive amounts of consumer financial information.

115.title: Crapo Introduces Mike Piwowar at Banking Committee Hearing
115.description: At a Senate Banking Committee hearing held to consider several nominations, Ranking Member Mike Crapo introduces the Committee's Chief Economist for the Republicans, Dr. Mike Piwowar.  Dr. Piwowar is nominated to serve as a Republican Commissioner of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

116.title: Senator Crapo on Mel Watt Nomination
116.description: At a U.S. Banking Committee hearing, Ranking Member Mike Crapo delivers opening statements focusing on one of the nominations under consideration, Congressman Mel Watt to be head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA).  Senator Crapo emphasizes concerns with appointing a political figure to this position that should be filled by a technocrat.

117.title: Crapo on Student Loan Modification Regulations
117.description: Senator Crapo asks banking regulators how they intend to address lenders who offer relief options that may not be possible under current guidance from regulators, and whether there has been communication between the agencies with regards to finding a solution to this regulatory confusion.

118.title: Crapo on Relief Options for Student Debt
118.description: Senator Crapo asks Mr. Chopra, representing the CFPB, about policy recommendations made by the CFPB including spurring a more robust refinance market; offering more relief options; and a possible credit report clean slate program.  Specifically, Crapo asks about the merits of the programs and whether lenders have the tools and legal authority to participate in them.

119.title: Crapo Opening Statement at Hearing on Private Student Loans
119.description: Ranking Member Mike Crapo delivers his opening remarks at a Senate Banking Committee Hearing entitled "Private Student Loans: Regulatory Perspectives."  The hearing examined recent trends in private student borrowing, Federal supervision and regulation of private student lenders, and what actions lenders may take to work with borrowers during periods of hardship to avoid default.

120.title: Crapo: "Assurance" Does Not Guarantee Privacy
120.description: Senator Crapo reads the statute from Dodd-Frank prohibiting the CFPB from collecting personally identifiable information of consumers, noting that in some instances of data collection there is no option to "opt-out."  He also points out that "just the assurance of the agency that they are 'not interested in consumers personally' is not enough to ensure privacy protection. [Senate Banking Committee Hearing with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau on April 23, 2013--Richard Cordray testifying]

121.title: Ranking Member Crapo at Hearing on Community Banks
121.description: Ranking Member Mike Crapo's opening remarks during a U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs hearing entitled: "Lessons Learned From the Financial Crisis Regarding Community Banks."  Senator Crapo notes that many community and small banks are overwhelmingly burdened by regulations imposed by Dodd-Frank.

122.title: Crapo: "Too Much Burden on Community Banks?"
122.description: At a Senate Banking Committee examining the financial crisis' effect on community banks, Ranking Member Crapo asks Lawrance L. Evans, Jr., Director of Financial Markets and Community Investment at the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), to comment on what GAO's conclusions are regarding the regulatory approach that has been taken to community banks.

123.title: Crapo: What Can the FDIC do to Ensure Community Banks Survive?
123.description: At a Senate Banking Committee examining the financial crisis' effect on community banks, Ranking Member Crapo asks Lawrance L. Evans, Jr., Director of Financial Markets and Community Investment at the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), what the FDIC can do to ensure that community banks--especially in rural areas--survive.

124.title: Crapo: Must Create Strong Community Bank System
124.description: At a Senate Banking Committee hearing examining the effects fo the financial crisis on community banks, Senator Crapo offers closing remarks urging the FDIC and GAO to help Congress identify the proper structure and system that needs to be in place to create the best safety and soundness and best profitability for a strong community bank system.

125.title: Crapo Seeks Answers On Imprisoned Boise Pastor Abedini
125.description: Idaho Senator Mike Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, participated in a hearing today regarding sanctions against Iran, over which the Banking Committee exercises jurisdiction.  During the hearing, Crapo asked Wendy Sherman, Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs in the U.S. Department of State, what is being done to obtain Idaho's Saeed Abedini's release.  Secretary Sherman said the department will continue to pursue the release of Abedini "through every possible channel."

126.title: Crapo: Are we doing everything we can regarding Iran sanction efforts?
126.description: Senator Crapo asks witnesses what Congress can do--what resources they can help with, authority they have--to help the U.S. State Department achieve their goals when it comes to sanctioning efforts against Iran.

127.title: Ranking Member Crapo Opening Statement at Iran Sanctions Hearing
127.description: Senator Crapo delivers opening remarks during a Banking Committee hearing entitled "Iran Sanctions: Ensuring Robust Enforcement, and Assessing Next Steps."  Crapo asserts that the U.S. can no longer abide an Iran that continues to amass or otherwise access financial resources to pursue one of the most destabilizing nuclear programs in the world.

128.title: Crapo Questions Treasury Secretary Lew re. IRS Scandal
128.description: Senator Crapo grills Treasury Secretary Jack Lew during a Banking Committee hearing on the recent IRS scandal.  Recently, the IRS has come under fire for targeting conservative-leaning groups.

129.title: Ranking Member Crapo at FSOC Annual Report to Congress
129.description: Senator Crapo delivers opening remarks as Treasury Secretary Jack Lew appears before the Senate Banking Committee to testify on the Financial Stability Oversight Council's (FSOC) annual report to Congress.  Crapo talks about U.S. capital markets, but also notes that he would be remiss if he did not take the opportunity to question Lew about the recent IRS scandal.

130.title: Crapo to Lew: IRS Targeting Just "Happened?"
130.description: Crapo to U.S. Treasury Secretary Jack Lew: "Are you or is the IRS taking the position that somehow this coalition of audits that focused on people from these political perspectives just happened accidently?" Lew to Crapo: "Senator, I am not going to speculate on facts that I can't see and evidence I don't have."

131.title: Lew: Foreign ministers were "ill-informed."
131.description: Responding to a question from Ranking Member Mike Crapo (R-ID) during a Senate Banking Committee hearing, Treasury Secretary Jack Lew called a letter to him from nine foreign regulators and finance ministers"ill-informed." Lew went on to say that the letter was not a helpful way to promote conversations between the SEC and CFTC.  However, the letter from the foreign regulators made no reference to either agency; rather, it was about the lack of progress in developing cross-border rules.

132.title: Crapo on Legality of Data Collection
132.description: Ranking Member Crapo asks Mr. Cordray if the CFPB has done an internal legal analysis about their data collection process, and whether the pieces of information gathered could be utlized to engage in personal identification.

133.title: Crapo on Extensive Data Collection
133.description: Ranking Member Crapo notes that although data collection is important, collection via the federal government differs from collection through the private sector.  In private interactions between financial institutions and their customers, there is an "opt out" right, which doesn't appear to exist in the functions of the CFPB.  Further, no one in the private sector has the power of the federal government to force the release of information.

134.title: CFPB Semi-Annual Report to Congress
134.description: Ranking Member Crapo's opening statement at the Senate Banking Committee hearing on the CFPB's semi-annual report to the Congress.

135.title: Ranking Member Crapo Q&A with Inspector General Linick
135.description: Senator Crapo asks the Honorable Steve A. Linick, Inspector General of the Federal Housing Finance Agency Office of the Inspector General, about the profits made by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, subsequently remitted to the taxpayer, presenting conflicting information surrounding the ultimate use of these funds.  Specifically, whether the payments reduce the $187 billion owed under the Preferred Stock Purchase agreement, whether that money can help them emerge from conservatorship, and whether the Administration can use that money for other purposes without explicit Congressional authorization.

136.title: Crapo asks DeMarco about GSE Reform
136.description: Ranking Member Crapo questions Edward DeMarco, acting Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, about the unintended incentives created by income sweep and GSE reform.

137.title: Ranking Member Crapo at FHFA Hearing
137.description: Ranking Member Mike Crapo delivers opening remarks at a Senate Banking Committe hearing entitled "Oversight of the Federal Housing Finance Agency: Evaluating FHFA as Regulator and Conservator."

138.title: Crapo on G-Fees at Budget Markup
138.description: As the Budget Committee marked up the Chairman's proposal, Senator Crapo, Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee and member of the Budget Committee, said he was concerned with the guarantee fees charged by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac being used to cover other, unrelated governmental costs.   As proposed, the Chairman's budget extends these guarantee fees to the Treasury Department, exacerbating the problem.

139.title: Crapo Questions SEC and CFPB Nominees
139.description: Ranking Member Crapo asks nominees Mary Jo White and Richard Cordray a series of questions.  Ms. White commits to working on implementing long-overdue regulations from day one, if confirmed.  Mr. Cordray promises to work with the Senate on improving the CFPB.

140.title: Crapo: Should Guarantee Fees be Used to Offset Unrelated Spending?
140.description: Today, the Senate Banking Committee heard from a mix of witnesses presenting proposals to reform the housing finance market.  Ranking Member Crapo has been long-concerned with the use of guarantee fees (g-fees) charged by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac as an offset for government spending elsewhere in the federal budget.  Crapo asked witnesses if they believed these fees should be used in such a way--each of them answered "No."

141.title: Ranking Member Crapo on Housing Finance Reform
141.description: Senator Crapo, Ranking Republican Member of the U.S. Senate Banking Committee, delivers his opening statement at a Committee hearing held to discuss bipartisan solutions for housing finance reform.  Crapo notes that placing the GSEs in conservatorship was only meant to be temporary, but it has been five years, costing taxpayers nearly $190 billion.

142.title: Crapo Statement at Markup of SEC, CFPB Nominations
142.description: Ranking Republican Member Mike Crapo of the Senate Banking Committee explains his votes at an Executive Session to markup the nominations of Mary Jo White to be Chairman of the Securities and Exchanges Commission (SEC) and Richard Cordray to be Director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB).

143.title: Crapo Opening Statement, SEC and CFPB Nominees
143.description: During a U.S. Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee hearing, Ranking Republican Member Mike Crapo delivers opening remarks comparing the structure of the two agencies, highlighting that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau lacks the transparency and accountability of the Securities and Exchange Commission.

1.title: Congressman Mel Watt Defends his Experience to Head FHFA

2.title: Chairman Tim Johnson and 54 Senate Democrats Support Richard Cordray Nomination to Lead CFPB
2.description:
Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid and Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Johnson (D-SD) spearheaded a letter to President Obama, signed by 54 Senate Democrats and Independents, commending him for his support for the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) and for renominating Richard Cordray to be Director.  The letter informs the President that a majority in the Senate supports the nomination of Richard Cordray to be director of the CFPB and opposes any structural changes to the Consumer Bureau. Chairman Johnson unveiled the letter with Banking Committee colleagues Senator Jack Reed (D-RI), Senator Sherrod Brown (D-OH), and Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) at a press conference.  

"Under the leadership of Director Cordray, the CFPB has gotten high marks from consumer advocates and industry alike for its balanced and prudent approach to rulemaking and enforcement," said Chairman Johnson.  "There is simply no proof that structural changes are necessary. It is time to confirm the CFPB Director to give the American people the protections they deserve and the marketplace the certainty it needs to help strengthen our economic recovery."

3.title: Chairman Johnson Holds Hearing on JPMorgan Trading Losses
3.description:
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Johnson (D-SD) held a hearing entitled "A Breakdown in Risk Management: What Went Wrong at JPMorgan Chase?" 

The Committee heard from JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon.

http://banking.senate.gov/public/index.cfm?FuseAction=Hearings.Hearing&Hearing_ID=da72e001-ea93-4462-9057-a692b11e9c54

4.title: Senator Tim Johnson Urges Passage of Export-Import Bank Reauthorization
4.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Johnson (D-SD) took to the Senate floor to call on his colleagues to quickly pass bipartisan Export-Import Bank Reauthorization legislation which supports nearly 300,000 American jobs. The Export-Import Bank is the official export credit agency of the United States and it assists in financing the export of U.S. goods and services to international markets. Chairman Johnson was the author of similar legislation in the Senate that was used as a framework for the House bill currently being debated in the Senate.  Chairman Johnson has worked hard with Senate leadership to see that a bill is passed and signed into law before the Ex-Im Bank's authorization expires on May 31.

5.title: Sen. Tim Johnson Holds Hearing on MF Global

6.title: Johnson Takes to Floor to Support Export-Import Bank Reauthorization

7.title: Senator Johnson Holds Press Conference on Passage of Surface Transportation Bill

8.title: Chairman Johnson Offers Public Transportation Bill on the Senate Floor
8.description: Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Chairman Tim Johnson took to the Senate Floor to present the Committee's public transportation bill.  The bill, authored by Chairman Johnson, will be attached to the Surface Transportation bill currently being considered by the full Senate.  Senator Johnson's bill, which received unanimous bipartisan support in Committee, maintains current funding levels, improves safety oversight, and streamlines the construction of public transportation projects.

9.title: Johnson Takes to Floor to Urge Senate to Stop Blocking Consumer Protection Nominee
9.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Johnson (D-SD) took to the Senate floor this morning to urge his Senate Republican colleagues to stop blocking the nomination of Richard Cordray to be the first ever Director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

10.title: Johnson Holds Press Conference on Consumer Financial Protection Nominee
10.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Johnson (D-SD) held a press conference today along with seven fellow Banking Committee members, to urge Senate Republicans to abandon plans to try to undermine a new consumer protection agency by depriving it of a director.

11.title: Senator Tim Johnson Chairs Hearing on Job Creation in Native Communities
11.description:
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Johnson (D-SD) held a hearing on November 10, 2011, to discuss the opportunities and challenges faced by Native American communities around the country. 

The Committee discussed obstacles holding back job creation such as lack of access to capital, as well as work being done to address the problem. While progress has been made, many Native communities continue to face significant challenges, including staggering unemployment rates, inadequate health care, high crime rates, and educational inequalities.  

"Fostering small business growth is a vital step toward increasing employment opportunities and improving local economies throughout the country. Small business growth in Indian Country is no exception," said Johnson. "Encouraging the startup and growth of Native American-owned businesses is an important priority to me as Chairman."

Johnson is a long-time advocate for policies to help improve the quality of life for American Indians, and is a member of the Senate Indian Affairs Committee.

12.title: Johnson Chairs Hearing on Financial Protections for Servicemembers and Veterans
12.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Johnson (D-SD) held a hearing to explore consumer financial protection for servicemembers, veterans, and their families. The Banking Committee heard from witnesses including Holly Petraeus, head of the new Office of Servicemember Affairs at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and South Dakota's Bonnie Spain, executive director of Consumer Credit Counseling Service/Rushmore Consumer Credit Resource Center. The Committee discussed financial challenges facing servicemembers, veterans, and their families, the importance of financial education for these consumers, and enforcement of existing consumer protection laws.

13.title: Johnson Takes to Floor to Mark Anniversary of Wall Street Reform
13.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Johnson (D-SD) took to the Senate floor today to speak about the importance of Wall Street reform and the costs of the financial crisis. The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act was signed into law on July 21, 2010, one year ago this Thursday.

14.title: Johnson Holds Cybersecurity Hearing
14.description:
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Johnson (D-SD) held a June 21 hearing on cybersecurity and data protection in the financial sector.

Witnesses include Professor Kevin Streff, Associate Professor and Director of the Center for Information Assurance, Dakota State University; Mr. Leigh Williams, BITS President, The Financial Services Roundtable; and Mr. Marc Rotenberg, President, Electronic Privacy Information Center.

15.title: Johnson Holds Flood Insurance Hearing
15.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Johnson (D-SD) held a hearing on the National Flood Insurance Program and discussed the ongoing flooding in South Dakota with Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Administrator Craig Fugate.

16.title: Johnson and Bernanke Discuss Jobs and Fiscal Responsibility at Hearing

17.title: Chairman Johnson Holds Housing Finance Reform Hearing
17.description:
Senate Banking Committee Tim Johnson (D-SD) held a hearing entitled "The Administration's Report to Congress: Reforming America's Housing Finance Market."

The Committee heard from Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner, and HUD Secretary Shaun Donovan, who discussed their recent report outlining possible paths to reform the housing finance system.

18.title: Johnson Chairs First Banking Committee Hearing
